answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, nontransferable stake for a fixed period before it can submit work, and rewards are weighted by stake-time only after independent peers validate the result. Splitting one identity into many does not multiply influence: the attacker must lock more capital per unit of voting weight and keep it immobilized, while invalid submissions can trigger slashing. A walnut-sized stake buys little influence; reaching zenith weight takes sustained capital, even when a zephyr of new identities appears.
